messages:
Priya: quick sync — we need a compact acceptance rubric for design partners that also captures jurisdictional gating (EU/US/APAC) and availability windows. goal: 3-week onboarding + 8-week feedback loop. :wave:
Anil: +1. Do we mean legal/regulatory gating (data residency, GDPR) or operational (SLA, maintenance windows)?
Priya: both. want to prevent late surprises for private/dedicated customers — capture upfront where they cannot host data outside region, and their preferred feedback cadence.
Sam: thinking we should add a simple availability matrix in intake: timezone overlap, committed engineers, weekly touchpoints, contract SLA. low lift but high signal.
Jia: for the rubric, propose 3 buckets: Eligibility (security/compliance), Commitment (time + signal), Fit (workload representativeness). each scored 0-3.
Beth: +1 Jia. also call out hard blockers vs negotiable items. e.g., hard blocker = must be able to sign DPA; negotiable = can accept monthly billing cycle.
Priya: here's a first draft checklist. paste into intake doc. feedback welcome.
Priya: ```
INTAKE CHECKLIST (one-liner answers)
- Region/jurisdiction: (US / EU / APAC / Hybrid)
- Data residency required? (Y/N + details)
- Requires private deployment? (Y/N)
- DPA/legal OK? (Y/N)
- Timezone overlap (hours/week)
- Dedicated eng contact (name + weekly hours)
- Primary workload archetype (chat/generation/embeddings/rerank)
- Success metric (latency p95, cost target, accuracy baseline)
- Preferred feedback cadence (weekly async / weekly sync / biweekly / monthly)
- Can commit to 8-week evaluation tasks? (Y/N)
- Escalation contact + SLA expectations
```
Anil: this is good. recommend adding 'rollback acceptance' — what they consider intolerable regressions so we can A/B and roll back.
Sam: also include a short micro-survey we'll run at weeks 2/4/8 to capture signal. short multiple-choice to keep response rate high.
Jia: sample micro-survey (2 items):
- "Did the integration meet latency & correctness expectations? (Yes / Mostly / Not yet)"
- "Would you recommend continuing to next phase? (Yes / Maybe / No)"
Beth: copy for legal: @legal-bot could you confirm if we need separate DPAs per region or if our standard DPA + SCCs is fine?
legal-bot: (automated) standard DPA + SCCs covers EU cross-border transfers for now. if customer requires local on-prem only, escalate to Legal for a bespoke agreement.
Priya: ok — mark 'DPA required' as hard blocker. next: scoring rubric. Jia, can you draft the 0-3 scoring definitions? keep it simple.
Jia: draft: 0 = fails requirement / disqualify. 1 = meets minimally, lots of caveats. 2 = good fit, some work. 3 = ideal. We'll weight: Eligibility x2, Commitment x1.5, Fit x1.
Sam: example calculation: score = floor((elig*2 + commit*1.5 + fit*1) / 4.5 * 10) -> normalized 0-10. propose threshold >=7 to accept.
Anil: love that. one more ops ask: capture maintenance blackout windows in intake so we can schedule rollouts without surprises.
Priya: noted. I'll update the checklist. final ask: who will own recruitment outreach and the initial screening call?
Beth: Product can handle screening for first 20 partners. Customer Success should join the screening call when DPA or private deploy is indicated.
Jia: timeline proposal: outreach (week 0-2), screening call + checklist (week 2), onboarding (week 3), eval (week 4-11), wrap & handoff (week 12).
Priya: sounds good. I'll update the intake template and add the micro-survey questions. tagging this thread to track changes. :thumbsup:
Sam: small note — add a prompt set and acceptance test harness to the onboarding so we can detect regressions automatically.
Priya: agree. will add to onboarding tasks. thanks all.
Beth: thanks — cc'ing @legal-bot for visibility.
legal-bot: (automated) logged: DP intake needs manual review when 'private deployment' = yes.
Priya: closing loop — I'll publish the checklist in the dp intake doc by EOW and ping for review.
Anil: great, thank you.
Jia: thanks!
Sam: :rocket:
